name: weekly-certification-references
title: Weekly Benefits Certification — help links and statutes
description: What stands behind the questions, bound to them by path. `audience` decides who sees a reference: `human` ones become the "Help me answer this question" link under the question; `agent` ones — the statutes — are for software helping someone fill the form (the Assistant card reads them through `formspec.field.help`) and never appear on the page; `both` shows to everyone. `target: "#"` binds to the whole form. `priority` orders them when a question has several; `type` says what kind of source it is.

references.title: How to certify for weekly benefits
references.description: A federal walkthrough of unemployment insurance, for anyone who wants the process in one place before answering.

references.title: 20 CFR 604.3 — able and available requirement
references.description: The federal rule the first question comes from: a claimant must be able to work, available for work, and actively seeking it to be paid for the week.

references.title: 26 U.S.C. 3304(a)(5) — refusal of suitable work
references.description: The federal statute behind the refusal question: conditions under which refusing new work may not deny compensation.

references.title: Reporting work and earnings for the week
references.description: How to report the week's work and earnings — part time, per diem, self-employment and gig work all count, and the pay reported is what was earned, not what was received.

references.title: Regular employment, self-employment, and gig work
references.description: What separates regular employment, self-employment and gig work for reporting purposes, since each is asked for differently.

references.title: 18 U.S.C. 1001 — false statements
references.description: The federal statute behind the certification checkbox: knowingly false statements carry penalties, which is why the form asks for an explicit attestation.
